correctness.rationale: The dyadic-block factor decomposition is exact and realizes all nine boundary phase pairs. Prefix count differences satisfy an elementary recurrence whose level-2 to level-8 shift and six-periodic Fourier coefficients prove every further six-step extension. Exact base rows imply both parity-dependent endpoints. Each prefix difference is a walk with increments in {-1,0,1}, and anchored intervals connect, establishing all intermediate integer counts. verify.py separately checks recurrence to k=120 and direct windows to k=10; experiments are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: Exact attainable letter frequencies at every dyadic length are a natural sharp one-coordinate invariant controlling possible Parikh vectors of a classical automatic word. The complete k+2-point contiguous support and logarithmic exact balance gap are structurally informative and not implied just by knowing the number of scalar additive weights. This supports abelian-complexity bounds without claiming a full classification.
